claims.text: Increasing atomic size mismatch in high-entropy alloys increases local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion enhances hardness and strength.
The proposed baseline is an equiatomic, single-phase CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
Cu is larger than Co in the atomic-size sense relevant to the proposed mismatch.
Partially replacing Co with Cu will increase atomic size mismatch in CrMnFeCoNi.
The baseline and modified alloys will be processed by the same melting, casting, and homogenization route.
Both compared alloys will retain a single-phase microstructure.
Mechanical testing will be performed at room temperature using identical strain rates.
Increased atomic size mismatch produces local lattice strains that obstruct dislocation motion.
Increased atomic size mismatch obstructs the nucleation of dislocations.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and nucleation increases resistance to deformation.
The Cu-substituted alloy will have higher Vickers hardness than baseline equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
The Cu-substituted alloy will have higher yield strength than baseline equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
The proposed governing behavior is limited to single-phase solid-solution HEAs under similar conventional processing and room-temperature conditions.
The hypothesis may not apply to multiphase or nanostructured HEAs or when other mechanisms dominate.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on the substitution level and resulting lattice distortion.
Competing strengthening mechanisms may affect the measured mechanical response.
Absence of a statistically significant increase in both hardness and yield strength is specified as a falsifying outcome.
Failure to confirm increased lattice distortion in the modified alloy is specified as a falsifying outcome.
